# Project plan

## Preliminary work

We have implemented an initial tutorialverse prototype supporting learnr, learnr2, and Quarto Live. The package validates common tutorial metadata, checks source and published URLs, and uses engine adapters to render trusted local tutorials while producing a common validation report. The [adapter review](https://github.com/tutorial-verse/tutorialverse/blob/3384ae6fd31f2f4d4538ced5cd9f02dc6aaa2216/prototype/adapter-review.md) documents successful renders of one public tutorial per engine on macOS. Interactive exercise execution and accessibility remain explicitly unsupported rather than being inferred from successful rendering. Cross-platform CI, curated registry records, and measurements of author effort remain proposed work.

## Schedule and working practices

| Period | Work and completion criteria |
|----------|----------------------------------------|
| Months 1–2 | Review the eight-field profile, map metadata from existing tutorials into pilot records, establish repositories and governance, and begin the reference fixtures. |
| Months 3–5 | Harden the three adapters and extend `check_tutorial()`. Publish a capability table and common report format. Test valid examples and known failures in Linux, macOS, and Windows CI. |
| Months 6–8 | Build registry ingestion and search. Publish `index.json` and the R search interface. Run the pilot records through the package and document author effort. |
| Months 9–10 | Pilot nominations and human review with external contributors. Test stale-entry handling and gather usability feedback. |
| Months 11–12 | Expand the registry to approximately 15 tutorials. Complete reference-fixture and integration-template checks. Address high-priority feedback and release version 1.0 of the package, specification, and registry with maintenance guidance. |

Development will occur openly on GitHub with pull-request review, automated testing, documented releases, and community updates. Code will use MIT; new educational content will use CC BY 4.0 where source licenses permit.

## Budget and funding

**Requested budget: USD 10,000**, for development, documentation, and review across the five milestones. No hardware, cloud, travel, or fee costs are included.

| Milestone | USD |
|-------------------------------------------|------:|
| Minimal metadata profile | 1,500 |
| Engine adapters | 2,500 |
| Validation package | 2,750 |
| Tutorial registry | 1,750 |
| Review, governance, and reference fixtures | 1,500 |
| Total | 10,000 |

If funding is reduced, the profile and validation tools can be used independently of the registry.

## Risks and maintenance

The prototype demonstrates the adapter model; adoption remains the main uncertainty. Authors may find the profile burdensome if it duplicates metadata they already maintain. The next experiment is the 5–10-tutorial registry pilot: we will record which fields are reused, supplied manually, or unknown, and measure author effort. These findings and early consultation will guide revisions before version 1.0.

Engine changes could break adapters or expose differences in test coverage. We will document supported versions and browser or server requirements, and use the reference fixtures to detect regressions.

We will document contribution and governance procedures so others can maintain the registry without relying on us for every change. Entries will name maintainers and retain source links, validation dates, and status. Scheduled checks and an archival policy will help contributors address stale resources.
